On-call chat (#sre-oncall)

  04:16  Ravi: node-alertd has been flaky before (it misfired twice in August on cache-07).
  04:17  Mei: Could be. The dashboard is our source of truth usually.

RUNBOOK RB-DB-12 "Disk alerts on database hosts" (last reviewed 2026-08-20)
  1. Metric sources. The "DB Fleet" Grafana dashboard is fed by metrics-agent v1, which only collects the ROOT volume ("/") of each host. Data volumes (/var/lib/postgresql) are monitored exclusively by node-alertd, and no dashboard panel shows them yet (ticket OBS-440).
  2. Known false positives: the August cache-07 misfires were caused by node-alertd reading a tmpfs mount; fixed in node-alertd 2.3.1 (rolled out to all hosts 2026-08-25).
  3. If the alert reports a data volume above threshold, treat it as real: start WAL/archive cleanup steps in §4.

Host facts: db-03 — root volume "/" 40 GB; data volume /var/lib/postgresql 2 TB (separate disk). node-alertd version on db-03: 2.3.1.

decision.instructions: Using only the information above, classify the pg-disk-high alert on db-03.

criteria.cannot_determine: The evidence genuinely conflicts and nothing in it resolves which reading is correct.
